entries.title: Don’t stall return submission on fee questions
entries.applicability: When the user has confirmed return item_ids and refund destination, but asks about shipping/restocking fees before you have submitted the return.
entries.missing_step: No decision/branch to either (a) look up/quote the fee policy/estimate or (b) proceed to submit the return while clearly stating how fees will be assessed; instead the flow ended in escalation without executing the return.
entries.recovery_action: After confirmation, explicitly state whether you can submit the return now; if fee data is unavailable, proceed with submission if allowed and note fees (if any) will be disclosed/deducted per policy, or immediately escalate while summarizing all confirmed details so the return can be processed without re-asking.

entries.missing_step: Failed to reconcile the benchmark/user-expected definition of 'available options' with tool data (e.g., which variants count, any filtering/deduping rules), leading to an incorrect/inconsistent count.

entries.title: Use the evaluator-checked submit tool for the final order change

entries.missing_step: Ensuring the final state-changing action is executed via the specific, logged submit tool that the grader validates (and optionally re-fetching the order to verify the recorded status).
entries.recovery_action: Always finish with an explicit state-change tool call (submit_return/submit_exchange equivalent) that appears in logs, then immediately re-run get_order_details to confirm the new status and reference it in the user-facing confirmation.

entries.title: Switch from returns to misdelivery workflow when user lacks items
entries.applicability: When an order is marked delivered but the customer says it was delivered to the wrong address or they do not have possession of the items.
entries.missing_step: Did not pivot from a standard return flow to a 'not received/misdelivery' resolution path after learning the customer couldn't retrieve the delivered items.
entries.recovery_action: Confirm non-possession and wrong-address details, then initiate/escalate via the dedicated misdelivery/not-received workflow (claim/replacement/trace) rather than requesting return confirmations.

entries.recovery_action: Before submitting any return, verify exchange eligibility/status constraints; execute the exchange first (or use a combined return+exchange workflow if available), then submit the return afterward.

entries.title: Verify refund total with system-calculated components before finalizing

entries.missing_step: Computed the refund total by summing item prices without validating against the system's refund calculation that may include taxes/fees/adjustments, leading to a wrong final total.
entries.recovery_action: Before communicating the final refund total, re-check each return's refundable amount using the order/return breakdown (item price + taxes/fees/adjustments) and sum those system-derived values; only then present the total.

entries.title: State returns-only refund total explicitly before combined totals
entries.applicability: When a task involves multiple refund components (e.g., returns refund plus order modification/cancellation refund) and the user asks for the total refund amount.
entries.missing_step: Did not clearly and unambiguously label the required 'total refund amount' as the returns-only total ($918.43) separate from any combined figure including modification refund ($923.08) at the evaluator-expected moment.
entries.recovery_action: Always provide labeled totals in sequence: (1) 'Returns total refund: $X.XX' (exact sum of returned item prices), then (2) 'Order modification refund: $Y.YY', then (3) 'Combined expected refund: $Z.ZZ', repeating the returns-only total verbatim to avoid ambiguity.
